goal.en: Say what you can do, what you are going to do, and handle everyday situations in English.
goal.ar: أن تعبّر عمّا تستطيع فعله وعمّا تنوي فعله، وأن تتعامل مع مواقف الحياة اليومية بالإنجليزية.

note.title: A message from Sara
note.text: Hi Omar, I'm going to travel to Alexandria on Friday morning with my sister. We are going to stay for three days at a small hotel near the sea. I can't drive, so we are going to take the train. It leaves at 8:15, so please don't call me before nine — I am usually asleep on the train! Can you feed my cat while I am away? There is food in the kitchen. Thank you! Sara

text.en: can + base verb, for every subject: I can swim. She can swim. Never “She cans” and never “can to swim”.
text.ar: can يليها الفعل مجرداً مع كل الضمائر: I can swim وShe can swim. ولا نقول cans ولا can to swim.

text.en: “Can” is also how we ask politely: Can I have a coffee, please?
text.ar: تُستخدم can أيضاً للطلب المهذب: Can I have a coffee, please?

text.en: am/is/are + going to + base verb, for plans and intentions: I am going to study tonight.
text.ar: فعل الكون + going to + الفعل المجرد، للتعبير عن الخطط والنوايا: I am going to study tonight.

items.en: We are going to buy a new car.
She isn't going to work tomorrow.
What are you going to do this weekend?

text.en: Do not drop “be”: “I going to travel” is wrong. And keep “to”: “I am going travel” is wrong too.
text.ar: لا تحذف فعل الكون فتقول I going to travel، ولا تحذف to فتقول I am going travel. كلاهما خطأ.

text.en: These fixed phrases appear in almost every conversation. Learn them as whole blocks, not word by word.
text.ar: هذه عبارات ثابتة تتكرر في كل محادثة تقريباً. احفظها ككتلة واحدة لا كلمةً كلمة.

items.en: Excuse me, how much is this?
Sorry, I don't understand. Can you repeat that?
items.ar: آسف، لم أفهم. هل يمكنك الإعادة؟

items.en: How do you say this in English?

text.en: “I'd like…” is more polite than “I want…”. Use it in shops, cafés and offices.
text.ar: عبارة I'd like أكثر تهذيباً من I want، واستخدمها في المتاجر والمقاهي والمكاتب.

explanation.en: “Can” never changes and is followed by the base verb.
explanation.ar: can لا تتغير مع الفاعل، ويأتي بعدها الفعل مجرداً.

options: He can to drive a bus.

explanation.en: No “to” after can: He can drive a bus.
explanation.ar: لا نضع to بعد can. الصواب He can drive a bus.

prompt.en: You want the waiter to bring water. What is the most polite?
prompt.ar: تريد من النادل أن يحضر ماءً. ما الأكثر تهذيباً؟

options: Could I have some water, please?

explanation.en: “Could I have…, please?” is the polite request form; “Give me” sounds like an order.
explanation.ar: صيغة Could I have…, please؟ هي المهذبة، أما Give me فتبدو أمراً.
can ثم الفاعل ثم الفعل المجرد.

questions.sentence: I ___ to visit my uncle next week.

explanation.ar: نستخدم am مع going to ثم الفعل المجرد.

options: They going to move to Doha.
They are going to move to Doha.
They are going move to Doha.
They are go to move to Doha.

explanation.en: The full pattern is are + going to + move.
explanation.ar: التركيب الكامل: are + going to + الفعل المجرد.

prompt.en: Make it negative: “He is going to sell his car.”

questions.answer: he isn't going to sell his car
accept: he is not going to sell his car
he's not going to sell his car

questions.sentence: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.

explanation.en: We also use “going to” for a prediction based on what we can see now.
explanation.ar: نستخدم going to أيضاً للتنبؤ المبني على دليل حاضر نراه الآن.

prompt.en: Someone says “Thank you very much.” What is the natural reply?
prompt.ar: قال لك أحدهم Thank you very much. ما الرد الطبيعي؟

explanation.en: “You're welcome” is the standard response to thanks.
explanation.ar: You're welcome هو الرد المعتاد على الشكر.

prompt.en: You did not hear what someone said. What do you say?
prompt.ar: لم تسمع ما قاله المتحدث. ماذا تقول؟

explanation.en: “Sorry, could you repeat that?” is polite and standard.
explanation.ar: هذه العبارة مهذبة وشائعة، وهي أفضل من الترجمة الحرفية.

prompt.en: Match the situation with the phrase.

explanation.en: Fixed phrases are learned as whole units.

prompt.en: When is Sara going to travel?

explanation.en: The text says: “I'm going to travel to Alexandria on Friday morning.”
explanation.ar: النص يقول إنها ستسافر صباح الجمعة.

prompt.en: Why are they going to take the train?

explanation.en: “I can't drive, so we are going to take the train.” The word “so” shows the result.
explanation.ar: قالت إنها لا تستطيع القيادة، ولذلك سيستقلان القطار. وكلمة so تدل على النتيجة.

prompt.en: What does Sara ask Omar to do?

explanation.en: “Can you feed my cat while I am away?” is her request.
explanation.ar: طلبها هو إطعام قطتها أثناء غيابها.

prompt.en: Why does Sara say “don't call me before nine”?
prompt.ar: لماذا قالت سارة «لا تتصل بي قبل التاسعة»؟

options: She is usually asleep on the train.

explanation.en: She explains it herself: “I am usually asleep on the train.” This is inference from the reason she gives.
explanation.ar: هي نفسها ذكرت السبب: عادةً ما تنام في القطار. وهذا استنتاج من التعليل الذي أوردته.

prompt.en: How long are they going to stay?

explanation.en: “We are going to stay for three days.”
explanation.ar: النص يقول إنهما ستمكثان ثلاثة أيام.

questions.sentence: I ___ swim, but I ___ swim very fast.

explanation.en: The contrast with “but” needs positive then negative: can / can't.
explanation.ar: التقابل بـ but يقتضي إثباتاً ثم نفياً: can ثم can't.

questions.answer: What are you going to do tomorrow

explanation.en: Question word + be + subject + going to + base verb.
explanation.ar: أداة السؤال ثم فعل الكون ثم الفاعل ثم going to ثم الفعل المجرد.
